name: Beechcraft King Air 90 series
variants: H90 / T-44 Pegasus (US Navy trainer, retiring)
summary: The original King Air, a compact twin turboprop in production since 1964 and the most common business twin turboprop in the US.

wings: Low, straight wing with the engines in nacelles on the wing
engines: Two PT6A turboprops in long nacelles with exhaust stacks pointing outboard
fuselage: Short cabin with a few rounded-square windows
Rounded nose; main gear retracts into the nacelles
tail: Conventional low-set tailplane with dihedral on most variants (the F90 has a T-tail)
Swept fin with a dorsal fillet

tellTales: Twin turboprop with its tailplane low on the fuselage, not on top of the fin
Short cabin with only a few windows
Engine exhaust stacks pointing outward from the nacelles

confusedWith.howToTell: The 90-series has a low-set tailplane (except the F90) and a short cabin; the 200/250/350 has a T-tail and a longer cabin.
The King Air 90 is larger with pressurized round-cornered windows and turboprop nacelles with exhaust stacks; the Baron is a smaller piston twin with short nacelles.
The King Air 90 is far shorter with a low tailplane; the 1900 is a long airliner with a T-tail and many small windows.
The King Air 90 has a rounder nose, a larger airliner-like cabin and no wingtip tanks; the PA-31T Cheyenne has a long pointed nose, a slimmer fuselage and usually wingtip tanks.
The PA-42 Cheyenne III/400 has a slim, long fuselage with small cabin windows and a T-tail; the King Air 90 (except the F90) has a low tailplane, larger windows and a shorter cabin.
The Conquest has small oval cabin windows and a long, tapered nose; the King Air 90 has larger rounded-square windows and a blunter, bulkier cabin.
